### Nostalgia[1]

A late aunt gave me a shell from a great or great uncle that took a trip to the South Pacific.* Seeing that triggers memories of trips taken and also how much I didn’t know about my aunt. When she received her terminal diagnosis I learned a lot about her life.

Triggers are a funny thing. They carry a negative connotation in certain circles, laden with meaning imbued from the Great Awokening around strong emotions activated, usually referenced through the past participle “triggered.” Such little memory activators are a very useful tool however for crafting one’s mind palace and a life.

I have a little sculpture of one of the robots from Star Wars the Phantom Menace on my desk. It’s made of old bike parts and reminds me to smile at the absurdity inherent in bureaucracy. I got it in Venice Beach. Little things like that are triggers too.

90s nostalgia is making a comeback as Millenials come into greater purchasing power. That was the focus of an Economist article. I have been cogitating on nostalgia in particular as it seems a powerful force in our era. The 21rst century is finally here, and the long lingering 20th is over, although we live in a time of monsters through the Gramsci Gap.[1] Politics in places like the US have been predicated on visions of the past during the past decade or so.

What constitutes the antithesis of nostalgia? Anticipation forms an eagerness for something in the future. That seems sort of funny too and reminds me of the quote about accepting the balance of time, the ripples from the past and the possibilities of the future, staying grounded in the present. 

***

*It’s funny as a bunch of family and friends think I’m a sort of mountain man adventure type though in many ways I find my adventure CV to be pretty tame. I suppose that probably speaks more to the mountains on my internal mental map?

***

[1] While writing this post, when I was about ~642 words in, I had to disconnect burrow and while the prompt said that the post would be saved locally, it's not showing up here sadly. I'm not sure if this is ironic although I do feel nostalgia for my little start of a post. Ha! 

[2] [The "Gramsci Gap" comes from Antonio Gramsci's line in his *Prison Notebooks*: "The crisis consists precisely in the fact that the old is dying and the new cannot be born; in this interregnum a great variety of morbid symptoms appear." It's more often quoted in its punchier paraphrase: "The old world is dying, and the new world struggles to be born: now is the time of monsters." The gap is that in-between stretch where the old order's institutions, assumptions and stories have lost their hold but nothing durable has replaced them yet. Into that vacuum rush the monsters: strongmen, conspiracy, nostalgia politics, all the strange things that grow when nobody quite knows what comes next. The [Monstrous Times]() substack takes its name and much of its outlook from that idea, and it's worth a read if you want someone thinking about this interregnum more rigorously than I'm doing here.]

***

Something I'd like to play with at some point is what's been called the other simulation hypothesis, which to my lay understanding, refers to the idea that emotions are part of the human intelligence system simulating alternative states.
